Rashi on Niddah 4a:10:1.hebrew: לשרוף - דלא מחזקינן טומאה ודאית ממקום למקום, לשרוף עליה תרומה:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:10:1.english: To burn - That we do not presume definite impurity from place to place, [so as] to burn terumah on its account.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:10:2.hebrew: אבל מתלא תלינן - דהרי משמע: במקום מציאתן הוא דחכמים מטמאין טומאה ודאי, אבל שלא במקום מציאתן טומאתן הוה ספק, ור' יוחנן נמי לתלות קאמר:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:10:2.english: But we indeed suspend - For it implies that it is [only] in the place of their discovery that the Rabbis deem [them] definitely impure, but not in the place of their discovery, their impurity is in doubt; and Rabbi Yoḥanan too was speaking of suspending [them].

Rashi on Niddah 4a:11:2.english: Or broken - [It was found] on top of ritually pure items, and he recognizes it [as having been] ritually impure.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:11:3.hebrew: טהורה - מלטמא טהרות שנמצאת עליהן, ולא אמרינן: שלמה נפלה עליהם וטמאתם, ואח"כ נשברה, אלא אמרינן: שבורה או חלודה, כאשר היתה עתה, נפלה עליהם. אלמ' כל הטמאות כשעת מציאתן מחזקי' להו, ואפי' תלייה ליכא, דקתני ״טהורה״. וקס"ד דה"ה נמי למקום מציאתן, דמחזקינן להו בטומאה, ולא מספקינן לה במקום אחר אפילו לתלות, וקשיא לר' יוחנן:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:11:3.english: Pure - From rendering impure the pure items upon which it was found; and we do not say: "It fell upon them whole and defiled them, and afterward it broke"; rather, we say: "Broken or rusty, as it was now, it fell upon them." Consequently, we presume all impurities [to be] as at the time of their finding, and there is not even suspension, as it teaches: "Pure." And [the Gemara] initially thought that the same applies also to the place of their finding: that we presume them to be ritually impure [only in that place], and we do not hold it in doubt in another place even to suspend; and [this] is difficult for Rabbi Yoḥanan.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:12:1.english: [If] it was found burned - [This refers to] the creeping animal.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:12:2.english: A rag - It was the garment of a zav.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:12:3.english: (Tattered) - The worn-out [rag]. [Meaning that] he found it worn out on top of olives.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:12:4.hebrew: טהורה - מלטמא הזיתים, דאמרינן: הכי נפלה עלייהו לאחר שבלתה וטהרה מטומאתה. אלמא לא מחזקינן טומאה משעה לשעה, אפי' לתלות, דקתני טהורה, וה"ה ממקום למקום:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:12:4.english: [It is] pure - [Meaning,] from defiling the olives, for we say that it fell upon them in this manner: after it had worn out and become pure from its ritual impurity. Evidently, we do not presume ritual impurity from hour to hour, even to hold [items] in suspension, as it teaches "[it is] pure"; and the same applies from place to place.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:13:1.hebrew: וכי תימא - לא דמי, דהכא משום הכי טהור, משום דשעת מציאתה ומקום מציאתה בטהרה הואי, דבתר שעת מציאתן אזלינן בין לקולא בין לחומרא: בין לקולא, כי הכא גבי מחט ומטלית, לאחזוקי בטהורה ודאי; בין לחומרא, כגון נגע באחד בלילה, לאחזוקי בטומאה ודאית:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:13:1.english: And if you would say - It is not comparable, for here, the reason it is pure is that the time of its finding and the place of its finding were in [a state of] purity, for we follow the time of their finding, whether for leniency or for stringency: whether for leniency, as here regarding the needle and the rag, to establish it as definitely pure; whether for stringency, such as [where one] touched someone at night, to establish it as definitely impure.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:13:2.hebrew: ושלא במקום מציאתן - דליכא רגלים לדבר כולי האי, משרף לא שרפינן, מתלא תלינן:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:13:2.english: And not in the place of their finding - Since there is not that much of a basis for the matter, we do not burn [teruma], but we hold [it] in suspension.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:14:1.english: The shelf - A board resting on pegs in the wall.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:14:2.hebrew: ומדף טמא - בגד טמא מונח תחת הדף בקרקע. בת"כ קרי מדף לעליונו של זב, ומדף לשון טומאה קלה הוא, כדלקמן. וס"ד השתא שהוא עליונו של זב, דטמא מדאורייתא; ומיהו טומאתו קלה משל מדרס, דלא הוי אב הטומאה לטמא אדם וכלים. ובא ומצא את הככר ע"ג הקרקע, מן הבגד והלאה:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:14:2.english: And an impure madaf - An impure garment lying under the shelf on the ground. In Torat Kohanim, it calls that which is above a zav "madaf," and "madaf" is a term denoting light impurity, as [the Gemara explains] below. And it enters [our] minds now that it is that which is above a zav, which is impure by Torah law; however, its impurity is lighter than that of midras, as it is not a primary source of impurity [av hatum'ah] to defile people and vessels. And [one] came and found the loaf on the ground, beyond the garment.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:14:3.hebrew: ונטלה - ולא נפלה. על גבי המדף - שנטלו מעל הדף, והניחה לארץ:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:14:3.english: And took it - And it did not fall. [As for] "upon the shelf" - That he took it from upon the shelf and placed it on the ground.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:15:1.english: It was only necessary - [This refers to] this [rationale of] "for I say."

Rashi on Niddah 4a:15:2.hebrew: אלא למקום מדרון - שאע"פ שהדף שהככר עליה מקום מדרון, וראויה הככר ליפול, ואם נפלה נגעה בבגד — אפילו הכי טהורה, שאני אומר כו'. אלמא, לא מחזקינן טומאה ממקום למקום, דנימא: מעל הדף נפל ונתגלגל לכאן:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:15:2.english: Only for an inclined place - That even though the board upon which the loaf rested was an inclined place, and the loaf was prone to fall, and if it fell it would have touched the garment, nevertheless it is pure, as [we say,] "I say..." etc. Evidently, we do not presume ritual impurity [to have transferred] from place to place, such that we would say: It fell from upon the board and rolled to here.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:2:1.hebrew: והא דומיא דאשה קתני - בההיא דהלל ושמאי, דקתני: מה הפרש בין זו לזו:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:2:1.english: But isn't it taught similar to a woman - In that [baraita] of Hillel and Shammai, which teaches: "What is the difference between this and that?"

Rashi on Niddah 4a:2:2.hebrew: ואשה בדוקה היא - מקודם לכן, דהא כל שחרית וערבית היא בודקת, אפ"ה טהרות דקופה טמאות, וקשיא לחזקיה:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:2:2.english: And a woman is examined - From beforehand, for she examines [herself] every morning and evening; even so, the ritually pure items of the basket are [ruled] impure, and [this is] difficult for Ḥizkiya.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:2:3.english: She is considered like [one who is] not checked - And with the basket as well, we are dealing with [one that is] not checked.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:3:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - הא והא בבדוקה, אלא דשמאי והלל כשאינה מכוסה ופיה מלמעלה, הלכך איכא למימר עם סילוק ידיו נפלו, וחזקיה במכוסה, מש"ה מטהר:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:3:1.english: And if you wish, say - Both this and that [case] deal with [a basket that was] examined. Rather, [the case of] Shammai and Hillel is when it is not covered and its opening is at the top; therefore, it can be said that with the withdrawal of his hands [a creeping animal] fell [in]. And Ḥizkiyya [deals with a basket that was] covered; for that reason he deems [it] pure.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:3:2.hebrew: מכוסה - בתמיה: היכי נפל האי שרץ, והיכי אישתכח בה השתא:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:3:2.english: Covered - [This is stated] in astonishment: How did this creeping animal fall [in], and how was it found in it now?

Rashi on Niddah 4a:3:3.hebrew: שתשמישה ע"י כסוי - כשהוא רוצה להכניס לתוכה ולהוציא מתוכה, מגלה ומכסה אותה. הלכך, חזקיה סבר: כל זמן שהטהרות בתוכה נזהר בה וכסה, והשתא, לאחר שניטלו ממנה, הסיח דעתו משמירתה ולא נזהר לכסותה, ונפל. ור' יוחנן סבר: חיישינן שמא כשגילה להשתמש בה, בעוד שהטהרות בתוכה, נפל:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:3:3.english: That its use is by means of a cover - When he wants to place [items] into it and remove [items] from it, he uncovers and covers it. Therefore, Ḥizkiyya holds: As long as the pure items were inside it, he was careful with it and covered [it], and now, after they were removed from it, he diverted his attention from guarding it and was not careful to cover it, and [the creeping animal] fell [in]. And Rabbi Yoḥanan holds: We are concerned that perhaps when he uncovered [it] to use it, while the pure items were [still] inside it, [the creeping animal] fell [in].

Rashi on Niddah 4a:4:1.hebrew: מכוסה היא - דלא נפיל בה דם מעלמא, וקופה דכוותה במכוסה עסקי', ואפ"ה טמאה, וקשיא לחזקיה:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:4:1.english: She is covered - For blood from the outside does not fall into her, and regarding a basket comparable to it, we are dealing with a covered [basket], and even so it is impure; and [this poses a] difficulty for Chizkiya.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:5:1.hebrew: בזוית בית - כדמפרש ואזיל, שטלטלה לקופה בזוית אחרת, לאחר שניטלו טהרות ממנה:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:5:1.english: In the corner of a house - As [the Gemara] goes on to explain, that one moved the basket to another corner after ritually pure items were removed from it.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:6:1.hebrew: ממקום למקום - דלא אמרינן: מאידך זוית הוה בה שרץ עם הטהרות, אלא אמרינן: לאחר שהביאה כאן נפל בה:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:6:1.english: From place to place - That we do not say: [Already] from the other corner there was a creeping animal in it with the ritually pure items; rather, we say: After he brought it [the basket] here, [the creeping animal] fell into it.

Rashi on Niddah 4a:9:1.hebrew: ובמקום מציאתן - אם מצאו שחרית מת באותו מקום שנגע בו בלילה, טמא; אבל מצאו במקום אחר מת, טהור, ולא אמרינן: כי היכי דהכא מת, התם נמי הוה מת במקומו הראשון:
Rashi on Niddah 4a:9:1.english: And in the place of their finding - If in the morning he found him dead in that place where he touched him at night, [he is] ritually impure; but if he found him dead in another place, [he is] ritually pure, and we do not say: Just as here he is dead, there too, in his first place, he was dead.

Tosafot on Niddah 4a:10:1.hebrew: ומי תלינן והא אנן תנן כו' - וא"ת: והיא הנותנת, משום דאזלינן בתר שעת מציאתה לגמרי, אפילו ממקום למקום לתלות, לכך מחט שנמצאת מלאה חלודה טהורה לגמרי. ואע"ג דמצינן למימר דהיינו דקאמר: וכ"ת כשעת מציאתן לגמרי בין לקולא בין לחומרא, מ"מ מאי ס"ד דמקשה? וי"ל, דס"ד: כיון דמחמיר כל כך בטומאה לתלות אפי' ממקום למקום [ע"כ אינו טעם גמור, דדוקא בקדשים הוא ומשום חומרא], א"כ במחט לא היה לו לטהר לגמרי משום שעת מציאתה, אלא הוה ליה למימר: השתא הוא דעלתה חלודה:
Tosafot on Niddah 4a:10:1.english: And do we suspend? But didn't we learn, etc. - And if you say: But that is the very reason [it is pure]: because we follow [its state at] the time of its discovery completely — even [if one holds that] from place to place we suspend — therefore, a needle that is found full of rust is completely pure. And even though we could say that this is what [the Gemara] means when it says: "And if you say: as at the time of their discovery completely, whether for leniency or for stringency..."; nevertheless, what was the questioner's initial reasoning? And one can say that it entered the questioner's mind: Since [the Tanna] is so stringent regarding ritual impurity so as to suspend even [when it moved] from place to place [perforce this is not a fully grounded rationale, for it applies specifically to consecrated items (kodashim) and on account of a stringency], if so, in [the case of] the needle, he should not have declared [it] completely pure on account of the time of its discovery; rather, he should have said: It is [only] now that rust formed [on it].

Tosafot on Niddah 4a:14:1.hebrew: ככר הנתונה על גבי דף - וא"ת: שאני התם, שאין בו דעת לישאל, כדאמר בסמוך? וי"ל, דפריך: אי בשום מקום אנו מחמירין ממקום למקום אפילו בקדשים, לא היה לנו לעשות ספק ולתלות באדם טהור, דיותר יש לתלות בנפילה:
Tosafot on Niddah 4a:14:1.english: A loaf resting on top of a shelf - And if you say: There it is different, because it lacks the capacity to be questioned, as [the Gemara] says nearby? One can say that [the Gemara] objects: If anywhere we are stringent [to suspect impurity moving] from place to place, even regarding consecrated items (kodashim), we would not have created an uncertainty and attributed [it] to a pure person, for it is more [reasonable] to attribute it to falling.

Tosafot on Niddah 4a:14:2.hebrew: שאני אומר אדם טהור - וא"ת: דהכא תלינן באדם טהור, ובפ"ק דחולין (דף ט:) גבי צלוחית שהניחה מכוסה ובא ומצאה מגולה, תלינן באדם טמא; וכן פ"ק דפסחים (דף י:) גבי קורדום? ותירץ ר"ת, דגבי כלים הנמצאין דווקא גזרינן טומאה, משום דאית להו טהרה במקוה וליכא פסידא; אבל באוכלין, דאיכא פסידא, דלית להו טהרה במקוה, לא החמירו. אי נמי, הכא מוכחא מילתא דאדם טהור הסירה בכוונה כדי שלא תפול על מדף טמא; אבל בעלמא טמאין, בין באוכלין בין בכלים, דליכא למימר אדם בכוונה עשה לתקנתא:
Tosafot on Niddah 4a:14:2.english: For I say a ritually pure person - And if you say: Here we attribute [it] to a ritually pure person, whereas in the first chapter of Chullin (9b), regarding a flask that one left covered and came and found uncovered, we attribute [it] to an impure person; and similarly [in] the first chapter of Pesachim (10b), regarding an axe? And Rabbeinu Tam answered that specifically regarding vessels that are found, we decree impurity, because they have purification in a mikveh and there is no financial loss; but regarding food, where there is a financial loss, as it has no purification in a mikveh, they [the Sages] were not stringent. Alternatively, here the matter is evident that a pure person removed it intentionally so that it would not fall upon an impure item (madaf); but generally [in other cases], they are impure, whether [in the case of] food or vessels, for it cannot be said that a person acted intentionally for the sake of rectification.

Tosafot on Niddah 4a:15:1.hebrew: לא נצרכה אלא למקום מדרון - פירוש, כשהמדף במקום מדרון, דאפילו נפל הככר על גבי מדף, לא נשאר לשם; אבל אם המדף בקרקע שוה, פשיטא דטהור:
Tosafot on Niddah 4a:15:1.english: It was necessary only for an inclined place - [The] explanation [is]: When the *madaf* [the impure object] is in an inclined place, for even if the loaf fell onto the *madaf*, it would not have remained there; but if the *madaf* is on level ground, it is obvious that [the loaf] is pure.

Tosafot on Niddah 4a:1:1.hebrew: כי פליגי חזקיה ור' יוחנן בקופה בדוקה - וא"ת, דבנגע באחד בלילה אמרו חכמים: אם ראוהו חי מבערב טהור, שספק טומאה ברה"ר ספקו טהור; משמע דברה"י, אפילו ראוהו חי — טמא! והשתא, הך קופה היכי דמיא? או ברה"ר — מאי טעמא דרבי יוחנן דמטמא? ואי ברה"י — מ"ט דחזקיה דמטהר? וי"ל, דברה"י איירי; וחזקיה יפרש הברייתא, דבראוהו חי מבערב טהור אפילו ברה"י, וספק טומאה ברה"ר טהור דקאמר — היינו דהוי כאילו הוא ספק טומאה ברה"ר, כיון שהיא בדוקה תחלה. ואגב דברישא נקט האי לישנא במילתיה דר"מ, היכא דלא ראוהו חי מבערב מתחלה, דקתני בתוספתא: ר"מ מטהר ברה"ר — נקט נמי במילתייהו דחכמים בסיפא רה"ר:
Tosafot on Niddah 4a:1:1.english: When Ḥizkiyya and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagree, [it is] regarding an examined basket - And if you say: But regarding [the case of] one who touched someone at night, the Sages said: If they saw him alive in the evening, [he is] pure, for [with] an uncertainty of ritual impurity in the public domain (reshut ha-rabbim), its uncertainty is [ruled] pure — which implies that in the private domain (reshut ha-yachid), even if they saw him alive, [he is] impure! And now, what are the circumstances of this basket? Either [it is located] in the public domain — [then] what is the reason of Rabbi Yoḥanan who deems [it] impure? Or if [it is located] in the private domain — what is the reason of Ḥizkiyya who deems [it] pure? And one can say that it is dealing with [a basket located] in the private domain; and Ḥizkiyya will explain the baraita, that [the ruling] that if they saw him alive in the evening he is pure [applies] even in the private domain. And that which it states, "an uncertainty of ritual impurity in the public domain is pure" — this means that it is as though it were an uncertainty of ritual impurity in the public domain, since it was examined initially. And incidentally, since in the first clause (reisha) it employed this phrasing in the statement of Rabbi Meir, where they had not seen him alive in the evening initially — as it is taught in the Tosefta: "Rabbi Meir deems [him] pure in the public domain" — it also employed "public domain" in the statement of the Sages in the latter clause (seifa).

Tosafot on Niddah 4a:4:1.hebrew: והא אשה מכוסה היא - פי' רש"י: דלא נפל בה דם מעלמא. וקשה, דכ"ש שהיא טמאה, דאין לתלות בדם אחר, אלא בא מגופה. לכך י"ל: מכוסה היא - שהמקום סתום, וכשהדם יוצא נפתח, והיה לה להרגיש. וא"ת: והא בקופה בדוקה פליגי, דאי לאו הכי, מאי מועיל כשהיא מכוסה? וא"כ, מאי פריך: והא אשה מכוסה? מאי מועיל כסוי, כיון דלאו כבדוקה דמיא? וי"ל, שרוצה ליישב אפי' אי חשיב לה כבדוקה:
Tosafot on Niddah 4a:4:1.english: And isn't a woman covered - Rashi explained that blood from the outside world does not fall into her. And this is difficult, for all the more so she is impure, since [the blood] cannot be attributed to other blood, but rather it came from her [own] body. Therefore, it can be said: "She is covered" [means] that the place is closed, and when the blood emerges it opens, and she would have felt it. And if you say: But surely they disagree regarding an examined basket, for if not so, what does it help that it is covered? And if so, why does [the Gemara] object: "And isn't a woman covered?" What does covering help, since she is not considered like an examined [basket]? And it can be answered that [the Gemara] wishes to resolve [the difficulty] even if she is considered as examined.

Tosafot on Niddah 4a:8:1.hebrew: שכל הטמאות כשעת מציאתן - לעיל פי' דהיינו דוקא לקדשים. והא דמחט שנמצאת מלאה חלודה דטהורה, דכל הטמאות כשעת מציאתן אפילו להקל, לאו משום דהוי כשעת מציאתן דאורייתא, אלא משום דמוקי הטהרות אחזקתייהו. וא"ת: מאי פריך מככר הנתונה על גבי דף, דלמא בככר של חולין איירי? וי"ל, דאפילו בחולין לא היה לנו לעשות כל כך לתלות באדם טהור, שהנפילה נראית יותר, והיה לנו לטמא ממקום למקום, כיון דלא אפשר ליפול אלא אם כן נגע, אי בשום מקום אנו מחמירין אפילו בקדשים:
Tosafot on Niddah 4a:8:1.english: That all impurities are as at the time of their finding - Earlier, [Tosafot] explained that this applies specifically to consecrated items (kodashim). And that which [a mishna teaches regarding] a needle that was found full of rust, that it is pure, as "all impurities are as at the time of their finding" even to be lenient — [this is] not because [judging] "as at the time of their finding" is by biblical law, but rather because we establish the pure items (teharot) upon their presumptive status [of purity]. And if you say: Why does [the Gemara] object from [the mishna regarding] a loaf placed on a board? Perhaps [that mishna] is dealing with a loaf of non-sacred food (chullin)! And one can say that even regarding non-sacred food, we would not have gone to such lengths to attribute [it] to a pure person, for falling is more likely, and we should have declared it impure [due to suspicion that it moved] from place to place, since it was impossible for it to fall unless it touched [the impure board] — if in any place we rule stringently [regarding impurity moving from place to place], even regarding consecrated items.
